residue.text: Retained ATT alternative: repeat fresh 300 rpm runs for exactly 60 seconds, without optical control or restart, sampling at second 120. Hypothesis: repeated sample success supports bounded dispensability of sustained 900 rpm. Rival prediction: failures or sampling-order dependence undermine reliable lower-speed sufficiency. This alternative competes with the six-trial paired-feedback plan; it cannot be added without reallocating trials.

Retained INV proposal: fixed 300/900 rpm, 60-second runs with matched imaging and quiet intervals; reverse speed order. If trials remain, matched pauses at seconds 45–50 and stopping at 65 preserve 60 stirring seconds. Hypothesis: prompt image improvement after cessation supports agitation-to-image influence. Persistent spread with successful vials favors an optical artifact; gradients with failed vials remain a rival. These tests require trial reallocation.

Preserved stage1 and concern limitations: enabled and timer runs have different quiet durations before second 120; record cessation times. Surface shape or settling can change images. Specks do not identify bubbles, and bubble fraction is unmeasurable. Sampling can disturb gradients; commanded rpm lacks independent verification; common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration. Equal final success cannot prove the hypothesized disturbance mechanism.

Preserve spill tray and stop if liquid escapes. Both arms failing, unchanged stirring duration, or inconsistent replication leave feedback benefit unresolved. Preferred total duration is unstipulated, so current time savings are unknown. Other materials, scales and continuous processes remain untested; no real chemical or human benefit is established.

summary.text: Observed synthetic evidence: one 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and yielded 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207 final attenuations, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and stable side checks for the bounded 4 percent sample proxy. Reliable sufficiency remains hypothetical; matched 900 rpm final samples are absent.

Stage1 and INV hypothesis: agitation causes optical disturbance; failed checks prolong agitation and renew disturbance. Rival hypothesis: genuine gradients cause failed checks and further stirring improves mixing. The rule, fluctuations and specks are stipulated; actual reinforcing-loop operation and speck identity remain unobserved.

Retain stage1 proposal: three fresh paired 900 rpm comparisons within six trials, alternating order. Fix 150 mL water, 0.30 mL dye, bottle, addition location and locked camera. Enable the preferred optical rule in one arm; stop the other at 60 seconds while logging shadow decisions. End all mixing by 105. Hypothesis: longer enabled stirring with both arms succeeding supports bounded feedback dispensability; timer failure with enabled success favors useful additional mixing.

Sample three elevations beginning at second 120, alternating withdrawal order. Report raw attenuation, normalized spread, stop times, stirring duration, shadow failures and every target failure. Record matched cessation images, depression and speck frames. Side-image stability alone cannot establish success; proposed interventions and predicted outcomes are hypotheses.
